Subject: [PATCH] RTL: Fix handling of special unicode marker 0xFEFF

This fixes a problem
in which the 0xFEFF mark was wrongly handled as RTL.

Change-Id: Icf8fce91e6df8c4fa8e01eb893174a9fdb8c0766

diff --git a/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java b/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java
index 88f725945..54bb57f0a 100644
--- a/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java
+++ b/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java
@@ -1692,7 +1692,7 @@ public class TextUtils {
                (c >= 0xFB1D && c <= 0xFB4F) ||
                (c >= 0x0600 && c <= 0x07BF) ||
                (c >= 0xFB50 && c <= 0xFDFF) ||
-               (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFF)    ;
+               (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFE)    ;
     }
 
     /**
-- 
2.48.1

## Summary

**File Modified:** `core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java`

**Modification:** In the method that determines whether a Unicode character is RTL (right-to-left), the boundary of one of the checked ranges was changed from `0xFEFF` to `0xFEFE`. Previously, the range `0xFE70` to `0xFEFF` was treated entirely as RTL characters, which incorrectly included the special Unicode character `0xFEFF` (the Byte Order Mark / Zero Width No-Break Space marker). This patch narrows the range to `0xFE70`–`0xFEFE`, excluding `0xFEFF` from being classified as RTL.

**Relationship:** This is a single-file, single-line fix. The change directly addresses the bug described in the commit message: `0xFEFF` was being wrongly identified as an RTL character due to its inclusion in the range check within the `isRTLCharacter` (or similarly named) method in `TextUtils.java`. By excluding this special marker from the RTL range, text direction handling for content containing this Unicode marker is corrected across the Android text framework, since `TextUtils` is a core utility class used throughout the system for text processing and directionality determination.

Here is the commit message:
RTL: Fix handling of special unicode marker 0xFEFF

This fixes a problem
in which the 0xFEFF mark was wrongly handled as RTL.

Change-Id: Icf8fce91e6df8c4fa8e01eb893174a9fdb8c0766

Here is the root cause:
The method used to detect right-to-left (RTL) characters in `TextUtils.java` checked whether a character code point fell within the inclusive range `0xFE70` to `0xFEFF` to classify it as RTL (this range corresponds to Arabic Presentation Forms-B). However, `0xFEFF` is a special Unicode code point known as the Byte Order Mark (BOM) / Zero Width No-Break Space, which is a formatting character with no inherent directional/script properties—it should not be classified as RTL. Because the range boundary was inclusive of `0xFEFF`, the code incorrectly treated this special marker as an RTL character, leading to incorrect text direction handling whenever this marker appeared in text. The fix corrects the upper bound of the range to `0xFEFE`, excluding `0xFEFF` from the RTL classification.

Here is the patch:
 
     public static boolean isRTLCharacter(char c) {
         //range of RTL characters per unicode specification
         return (c >= 0x0590 && c <= 0x05FF) ||
                (c >= 0xFB1D && c <= 0xFB4F) ||
                (c >= 0x0600 && c <= 0x07BF) ||
                (c >= 0xFB50 && c <= 0xFDFF) ||
-               (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFF)    ;
+               (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFE)    ;
     }

Reason:
The range check `c <= 0xFEFF` includes the special Unicode code point `0xFEFF`, which is the Byte Order Mark (BOM) / Zero Width No-Break Space. This character is a formatting marker with no inherent directional property, but because the upper bound of the Arabic Presentation Forms-B range was inclusively set to `0xFEFF`, the method incorrectly classified it as an RTL character, causing wrong text direction handling whenever this marker appeared in text.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
`return (c >= 0x0590 && c <= 0x05FF) || (c >= 0xFB1D && c <= 0xFB4F) || (c >= 0x0600 && c <= 0x07BF) || (c >= 0xFB50 && c <= 0xFDFF) || (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFE);`
Reason:
By changing the upper bound of the last range from `0xFEFF` to `0xFEFE`, the special marker `0xFEFF` is now excluded from the RTL character range, ensuring it is correctly treated as a non-RTL formatting character rather than being wrongly classified as part of the Arabic Presentation Forms-B script range.
